start_here: Say to your AI: "Make my voice from the recording Voice/Me talking.wav." It runs tool:voices with {"recording":"Voice/Me talking.wav"}, which answers the voice row and its reference sound; your AI keeps that row in your Voices list.

lists.label: Voices
lists.holds: One voice the person can be spoken to in: a shared voice or one made from their own recording, and how fast it talks.
alike: the voices list in a text-to-speech app
a spreadsheet of voice names and speeds

lists.label: Where Trillion speaks
lists.holds: One place Trillion talks to the person or for them, the voice it uses there and how fast.
alike: a table of where each voice is used

instructions: 1. Your voices and the places Trillion speaks are the rows of list:voices and list:where-trillion-speaks. Your AI reads and writes them in a store (it calls that store's own tool server); tool:voices never touches them.

2. To add your own voice, have a recording of you speaking on this computer and say "Make my voice from Voice/Me talking.wav": the AI runs tool:voices with {"recording":"Voice/Me talking.wav","label":"Your own voice"}. It picks 5 to 12 seconds that start after a pause and end on a sentence, and hands back the reference sound (the run's declared output) and the row { id, values }.

3. Your AI keeps the returned row in your Voices list with `reference` set to where the reference sound sits on this computer, marks the voice Chosen if you want it to speak, and switches or removes voices the same way, in the store.
4. Read the answer: voice (the row), file and files (the reference sound) and said (one plain sentence). Then run tool:say-with-a-voice-model with your Voices rows handed in to hear it.

worked_examples.title: Make a voice from your own recording
worked_examples.ask: Make my voice from my recording.
worked_examples.given: From tools/generate-speech/test/speak.test.mjs (the tool:voices test): a recording on this computer and a stand-in speech model that answers the words in it.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"voice":{"id":"own-...","values":{"label":"Your own voice","engine":"qwen3-tts","reference_text":"Every word of it.","made_from":"Voice/Me talking.wav","made_at":"..."}},"file":"1f:...","files":[{"name":"reference.wav","bytes":4,"blake3":"..."}],"said":"Your voice was made from 9.1 seconds of Voice/Me talking.wav."}. With no recording it answers the error "Give a recording of the person speaking (a file on this computer) to make their voice from.".

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and its fields. The tool matches each kit field to one of yours (by the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than least_coverage of the kit's fields match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the example rows to your list, leaving your own rows untouched.
